overall_summary: The channel is experiencing its highest engagement and view velocity with extreme cosmic anomalies and mind-bending space facts, while psychology, brain hacks, and repetitive re-uploads of memory-related content are severely underperforming. Space-themed videos average significantly higher views than any other category.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' reached 874 views, 'The Largest Ocean in Space' reached 460 views, and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' reached 368 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space concepts that present a physical paradox or sensory mismatch (e.g., hot ice, space smells, liquid metal rain).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' reached 302 views, 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' reached 183 views, and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' reached 179 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce highly visual, short-form animal facts focusing on survival mechanisms or ancient evolutionary anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' stalled at 54 views (and 5 views on a duplicate upload), while 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on generic brain/psychology facts and avoid direct re-uploads of identical titles, as they fail to trigger the Shorts algorithm.

next_video.opening_direction: There is a giant planet in our galaxy where the weather forecast is literally a downpour of liquid iron.

next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high performance of extreme planetary weather conditions (like the burning ice and glass rain videos) using a highly visual, terrifying cosmic concept.

experiment: Test a 'Space vs. Earth' comparison format (e.g., comparing Earth's most extreme environment to a cosmic equivalent) to bridge the gap between earth science and space enthusiasts.
